import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Congruences $a(n+k) \equiv a(n) \pmod k$ for hypergeometric values ${}_2F_1(n, -n; ; -1)$

a: $a(n) = \text{hypergeometric}([n, -n], [], -1)$.
This is equivalent to the combinatorial sum:
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k-1}{k} k!$$
The expression uses $\mathbb{N}$ arithmetic throughout, safely handling
the subtraction via `Nat.pred`.

*References:*
- [A278070](https://oeis.org/A278070)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA278070


open Nat Finset

/--
a: $a(n) = \text{hypergeometric}([n, -n], [], -1)$.
This is equivalent to the combinatorial sum:
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k-1}{k} k!$$
The expression uses $\mathbb{N}$ arithmetic throughout, safely handling
the subtraction via `Nat.pred`.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (n + 1)).sum fun k =>
    (n.choose k) * ((n + k).pred.choose k) * (k.factorial)


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 2 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 11 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 106 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 1457 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: $a(n+k) \equiv a(n) \pmod{k}$ for all $n$ and $k$. - _Peter Bala_, Mar 12 2023

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/278070.wip.lean#L68"]
theorem a_modeq : ∀ (n k : ℕ), Nat.ModEq k (a (n + k)) (a n) := by
    sorry

end OeisA278070

findings.description: The module heading at line 20 labels the sequence as ${}_2F_1(n,-n;;-1)$. There are two numerator parameters and no denominator parameters, so this should be ${}_2F_0$. The subsequent prose, definition `OeisA278070.a`, and theorem correctly describe the OEIS sequence; only the heading is wrong.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A278070 defines `a(n) = hypergeometric([n, -n], [], -1)` and explicitly lists the binomial sum used in Lean. Read in the official data mirror at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A278/A278070.seq. DLMF equation 16.2.1, https://dlmf.nist.gov/16.2.E1.tex, defines the subscripts p and q as the numbers of numerator and denominator parameters.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `${}_2F_1(n, -n; ; -1)$` in the module heading with `${}_2F_0(n, -n; ; -1)$`.

reformulations.difference: The hypergeometric definition is implemented as a finite sum of natural-number binomial coefficients and factorials, with `Nat.pred` for the upper index n+k−1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The defining hypergeometric term is (n)_k(-n)_k(-1)^k/k!. Terms with k>n vanish, and the remaining terms equal binomial(n,k)·binomial(n+k−1,k)·k!. OEIS explicitly gives this same finite-sum formula. At n=k=0, replacing the generalized binomial(-1,0) by `0.choose 0` preserves its value 1. In /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, I proved termwise equality over ℚ, vanishing beyond n, and equality of `a n` with the full Pochhammer-defined hypergeometric series, without using the conjectured congruence or any sorry.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the seven declarations. All 19 displayed OEIS terms and its modulo-7 example match Lean evaluation; no congruence failures occurred for 0 ≤ n,k ≤ 40. The zero-modulus case is reflexive, and its harmless inclusion was proved in Lean. The `research solved` status agrees with OEIS's May 31, 2026 proof announcement and the follow-up paper. The exact linked proof has the same definition and statement and no explicit sorry or custom axioms, but its historical Mathlib APIs prevented a successful kernel replay under the installed toolchain; this is not evidence of a mathematical or status discrepancy.
